headline: Large Energy User Grid Cost Shifting
short_summary: This bill directs Dominion Energy Virginia to propose rate structures that allocate costs for increased generating capacity and distribution infrastructure to large energy users (25 MW or greater), preventing these costs from being passed to other customers.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP1123) on 2026-05-14
opponents: Data center industry, large industrial energy users
news_headline: Virginia Shifts Data Center Energy Costs to High-Demand Users
news_summary: New legislation in Virginia requires data centers and other high-demand energy users (25 MW or more) to pay for increased generating capacity, preventing these costs from being passed on to other customers. This move is part of a broader legislative focus in 2026 on data center impacts in the state.

headline: Data Center Water Consumption Reporting
short_summary: This bill mandates water utilities to report the total volume of potable and reclaimed water provided to data centers monthly, enhancing transparency on water usage.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP0896) on 2026-04-13
supporters: Environmental groups, water conservation advocates, local communities
news_headline: Virginia Legislators Pass Data Center Water Usage Reporting Requirements
news_summary: Virginia lawmakers passed SB 553, requiring water utilities to report monthly water volumes supplied to data centers, including potable and reclaimed water. This legislation aims to provide greater clarity on data center water consumption and its environmental impact.

headline: Data Center Siting and Noise Limits
short_summary: This bill establishes a permit process for high energy use facilities (100 MW or more), requiring site assessments for sound profiles near residential areas and schools, and allowing localities to assess impacts on water, agriculture, and historic resources.
status: Last Action: Incorporated by Counties, Cities and Towns (HB153-Thomas) (Voice Vote) on 2026-01-23
supporters: Local communities, residents near proposed data center sites, environmental groups
opponents: Data center developers, real estate industry
news_headline: Virginia Passes Data Center Siting Restrictions and Noise Assessments
news_summary: HB 153, passed by the Virginia legislature, creates a permit process for high energy use facilities, mandating sound assessments near homes and schools. It also grants localities the power to require assessments of environmental and historical impacts before approving data center projects.
